23 A wire of length L is stretched to determine its limit of proportionality.
The graph shows the variation of the extension x with the force F applied to the wire.
F
P
0
0
x
The limit of proportionality is shown by point P on the graph.
The experiment is repeated with another wire of length 2L but of the same material and same
diameter as the first wire.
Which point on the graph shows the limit of proportionality for the new wire?
F
B
D
C
A
P
0
0
x

hints: Notice the axes are $F$ vertical against $x$ horizontal, and the new wire has length $2L$ with the same diameter and same material as length $L$.
Recall $stress = F/A$ and $strain = x/L$, so the limit of proportionality is fixed by the same limiting stress and same limiting strain for the same material.
Compare what stays the same and what doubles: same $A$ gives same $F$ at the limit, while same $x/L$ with doubled $L$ gives doubled $x$.
walkthrough: Identify the given change: length $L$ to $2L$, with cross-sectional area $A$ and Young modulus $E$ unchanged because material and diameter are the same.
State the rule for the material limit: proportionality ends at a fixed limiting stress $\sigma = F/A$ and fixed limiting strain $\epsilon = x/L$.
Apply same area: $F = \sigma A$, so the force $F$ at point P is unchanged for the new wire. The new point must lie on the horizontal line through P.
Apply doubled length: $x = \epsilon L$, so for the same $\epsilon$ the extension at the limit is $x_{new} = 2x_P$. The new point must be twice as far along the $x$-axis.
Check the $F$-$x$ stiffness: from $E = FL/(Ax)$, the gradient $F/x = EA/L$ halves for $2L$, so the new proportional line is less steep and reaches the same $F$ at $2x$.
Point D is the only point with the same $F$ as P and larger $x$ by a factor of about two. This is option D

A.explanation: Point A is at the same $F$ and same $x$ as P, but a wire of length $2L$ stretches twice as much for a given $F$ so its limit must be at larger $x$.

B.explanation: Point B is at about twice the $x$ but at a much larger $F$ than P, whereas the force at the limit does not change when only length is changed.

C.explanation: Point C is at smaller $x$ than P, which would mean a longer wire is stiffer, opposite to $x = FL/(AE)$ for the same $F$.

D.explanation: Point D has the same $F$ as P but about twice the $x$, matching the same limiting stress and same limiting strain for length $2L$.
